chunks: ʿAlī ibn Ibrāhīm, from his father, from Ibn Abī ʿUmayr, from Ḥusayn ibn Aḥmad al-Minqarī, from ʿĪsā al-Ḍaʿīf, who said:

I said to Abū ʿAbd Allāh عليه السلام: A man killed another man intentionally; what is his tawbah? He said: “He should submit himself.” I said: He fears that they will kill him. He said: “Then let him give them the diyah.” I said: He fears that they will come to know thereby. He said: “Then let him marry a woman from among them.” I said: He fears that she may inform them of that. He said: “Then let him consider the diyah, make it into purses, then watch for the times of salat, and let him cast it into their house.”

key_terms.الدِّيَةَ: blood money; the financial compensation due to the victim’s heirs
key_terms.تَوْبَتُهُ: his repentance; the required return from the sin in this legal context
key_terms.دَارِهِمْ: their house; the home of the slain man’s family
key_terms.صُرَرًا: purses or tied bundles; a way of packaging the compensation discreetly
key_terms.مَوَاقِيتَ الصَّلَاةِ: the times of salat; specific prayer times used here as a practical moment for delivery
key_terms.يُمَكِّنُ مِنْ نَفْسِهِ: he submits himself; he places himself at the disposal of the legal claim

ai.seo_question: What is the tawbah for someone who intentionally killed another person according to Imam al-Ṣādiq عليه السلام?
ai.summary: This hadith discusses the tawbah of one who intentionally committed murder, directing him first to submit himself for just requital. If he fears that, he is instructed to ensure the diyah reaches the victim’s family, even by a concealed means, showing the gravity of the crime and the necessity of restoring the right due to others.
